subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 07, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 07, 2026

Welcome to your Monday morning dose of AcreetionOS news. This week we're celebrating another smooth week of development as the team continues refining our Arch-based Linux distribution with privacy and stability at its core. Whether you're a seasoned Linux user or just discovering what a Cinnamon desktop can do, we're glad you're here.

On the development front, the Xlibre build received a small but important update this week with the addition of Firefox-ublock-origin to the default installation. This ensures users have ad-blocking capabilities built right in from the first boot, complementing the privacy-focused philosophy that drives AcreetionOS. Darren and Natalie have also been working behind the scenes to resolve a geocode-glib update conflict in the release branch.

The CI/CD pipeline for the AcreetionOS server infrastructure got some love as well. A new welcome message for first-time contributors was added to help onboard anyone interested in contributing to the project. Additionally, ShellCheck linting is now integrated into the shell script validation process, which means better code quality and fewer bugs making it into production.

The team completed their regular intelligence sync, pushing updated newsletter archives and wiki guides across both September 5th and 6th. This regular maintenance ensures that documentation stays fresh and community resources remain accessible. If you haven't checked out the wiki recently, head over to acreetionos.org for the latest guides.

From the broader Linux community, Grml released version 2026.09 this week, continuing to demonstrate the vibrant ecosystem surrounding Debian-based and Arch-based distributions alike. Staying informed about what other projects are building helps the AcreetionOS team draw inspiration and avoid reinventing the wheel.

Security advisories were issued Friday by Debian and Fedora covering various packages including Chromium, Firefox ESR, and several kernel updates. While AcreetionOS is built on Arch Linux's rolling release model which typically delivers security patches quickly, we always encourage users to keep their systems updated regularly. Running sudo pacman -Syu periodically is your best defense.

If you've been meaning to contribute to AcreetionOS, now is a great time to get involved. The team has made it easier than ever to start contributing with the new first-time contributor welcome message in the server repository. Whether you're interested in documentation, testing, or coding, there's a place for you in the community.

Speaking of getting involved, our Discord server at discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7 remains the best place to connect with fellow users and the development team directly. It's also worth following us on Bluesky at bsky.app/profile/acreetionos.bsky.social and X at @acreetionos for real-time updates and community interaction.

For today's tip: if you're experiencing any issues after updating your system, try checking the wiki's troubleshooting guides before posting in Discord. Many common problems have already been documented, and a quick search might save you time. The community is also very active in answering questions, so don't be shy about asking.

That's all for today, folks. Keep your systems updated, your privacy protected, and your terminals ready. We'll see you tomorrow with more AcreetionOS updates.
